definition: In image processing, computer vision and related fields, an image moment is a certain particular weighted average (moment) of the image pixels' intensities, or a function of such moments, usually chosen to have some attractive property or interpretation.
details: Image moments are useful to describe objects after segmentation. Simple properties of the image which are found via image moments include area (or total intensity), its centroid, and information about its orientation.

explainer.lead: An image moment is a weighted average of pixel intensities, or a function of such moments, chosen for a useful property. Moments let you describe objects after segmentation.

tiers.eli5: Like summarising a shape by its average position and how it is spread out, instead of listing every dot.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers compute moments to get area, centroid and orientation cheaply; a common pitfall is that simple moments are sensitive to noise and to how the object was segmented.
tiers.paperLevel: A weighted average (moment) of the image pixels' intensities, or a function of such moments; simple properties found via moments include area (total intensity), centroid, and orientation information.

explainer.example: Computing an object's area, centroid and orientation from its image moments after segmentation.
